matched: Water treatment technological development brings prominent energy consumption and carbon emissions challenges
Traditional processes face technical and economic constraints: adsorption regeneration is difficult, photocatalysis is limited by efficiency, microwave catalytic equipment cost is high

Coagulation operating cost accounts for high proportion of total water plant cost; traditional empirical models fail to balance dosing accuracy and energy efficiency due to nonlinear dynamics, multivariate variation (temperature, pH), and real-time disturbances
Determining optimal coagulant dosage based on raw water quality and treated water quality criteria is critical for effectiveness and economic/environmental benefits
Traditional manual dosing is subjective, consumes high drug amount, cannot adapt to large scale, causes unstable water quality and regulatory lag
Mechanistic models struggle with complex reactions and nonlinear relationships in coagulation, limiting practical applicability
Data-driven ML models construct black-box representations for nonlinear multivariate dynamic systems from limited data, but suffer generalizability and convergence limitations in coagulant dosing
Existing coagulation prediction methods have specific limitations: DL-MV relies on parameter tuning; PSO-SVR requires manual preset parameters; GA-RF has hardened architectures and high compute cost
Existing methods share two core limitations: reliance on manual intervention and single optimization paradigm lacking dynamic synergistic mechanisms
AutoML builds efficient ML pipelines by automating the entire process; distributed frameworks like TPOT reduce development costs and labor dependency
AutoML excels in hyperparameter optimization and complex constraint solving

AutoML demonstrates superior water quality performance: TPOT improves accuracy by 15-20% on 50D data; H2O predicts biological nutrient removal in wastewater; TPOT outperforms traditional ML by 1.4% in lake water classification
AutoML exploration and application in coagulant dosing prediction have not yet been extensively pursued
Advanced ML black-box nature limits interpretability, hindering practical adoption in water plants where operational transparency is critical
SHAP method (Lundberg & Lee) improves transparency, credibility, and decision making by quantifying marginal contributions and feature interactions globally and locally
SHAP has been successfully applied to surface water quality prediction, but not yet to coagulant dosage prediction
This study is the first to apply interpretable AutoML with SHAP to coagulation dose prediction, combining real-time and historical data for accurate control and treated water standards compliance
